key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while the multitask neural network offered strong shared-learning performance across related welding targets.
engineering_relevance: The study helps welding engineers choose between a shared multi-output model for efficiency and an ensemble model for maximum task-specific prediction accuracy in process optimization and quality control.
method: Compared multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding properties: UTS, weld bead hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated models using RMSE and R² on the same shared dataset.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower RMSE and higher R² for stacking across all three targets, with especially strong results for UTS and weld hardness.
watch_item: Performance is reported on one dataset, so model generalization to other welding materials, joints, or process settings should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
